insights.title: Context not content, one layer apart
insights.text: You standardize the context AI acts on. I standardize the decision a human commits to. Same move, one layer up. You said it yourself on the call: what I do for a person is what you do for the data.

insights.title: The same architecture, from opposite ends
insights.text: Yours is one human reviewing the work of many AIs, end to end. Mine is one human steering a decision engine. Neither of us set out to copy the other, and we landed in the same place.

insights.title: The shared bet
insights.text: Under both companies is one wager: structured, portable context beats more compute. Your one activity table and my one receipt table are the same bet, that the bottleneck is not model quality, it is context that can move.

insights.title: The quiet one: statefulness
insights.text: Most orgs never close the loop between a decision made downstream and the context it leaves stale upstream. Both our systems exist because that loop is open.

insights.title: [internal only] generosity / role / channel reads

header.title: Recoil Report, our call
header.sub: Run on our own conversation, Jul 22. The same analysis I would run on one of your customers' sales-call timelines.

blocks.h2: What this is, in your language
p: It turns a conversation into a time-ordered model of what each side believed and how those beliefs moved as new information arrived. Same shape as your activity schema, pointed at decisions instead of rows. Expected versus actual, joined on time.

You put it well on the call: the customers who care about revenue and have real data problems are also the ones making expensive, hard-to-reverse decisions. That is exactly who this is for. Your data may be the less interesting part. Your customers' need is the interesting part, and it is a strong fit.

blocks.h2: The capabilities, at a high level
blocks.intro: Enough to see the shape. The specific model and operators are held back, so this is what it does, not how it is tuned.

items.html: Tracks each claim as a credence that updates over the call, plus how settled that estimate is. It can tell a belief that has locked in from one still in motion.

It pressure-tests its own reads before trusting them. Each conclusion gets red-teamed and pre-mortemed against itself, and only what survives the attack gets reported. The number you see is the one that already held up under fire.
It gets sharper from being wrong. A read that turns out false is the highest-information event in the log, so the system keeps the correction instead of smoothing it over.
Resolution builds as the log grows. More calls make it sharper, the same way more activities make your table more answerable.

rows: One activity table, queried for any answer
one receipt table, queried for any bearing
Temporal join, time + entity, no foreign keys

Single source of truth, model once

blocks.text: Watch it work, traced on our own call

blocks.intro: Two claims tracked across our call. One of them is a belief of mine that collapsed, which is the honest part. The engine caught the correction instead of hiding it.
blocks.close: The cyan line is a prior I walked in with, that your media proposal was the thing you wanted to work on. It held flat, then dropped hard when you corrected it. That one correction carried most of the update, and the claim closed low and settled. The green line is the overlap between us, which started as a guess and rose to a confident read on your own framing.

blocks.h2: Why being wrong is the point
p: The value is not that the model was right. When I was wrong, it caught the correction and kept it, instead of quietly editing it out. That is the same property your one table has: every activity you append makes it more answerable, not more brittle. The honest diff is worth more than a flattering summary.

blocks.intro: The point of a pass like this is not the obvious summary. It is the quiet signals underneath. Four that came out of our call, on four different planes.

p: Pick one of your customers with a lot of sales calls. We take their existing customer-journey timeline, run this on it, and produce one sponsored report with your name on it. One customer, existing export, no new integration. Per-customer and aggregate both work, so we start with one and widen.

A fixed pilot fee, scoped to that one customer. I will put the number on it the moment we pick who, so it stays honest to the real scope. Free single run per company, then they talk to me. If it lands, it becomes a repeatable add-on across your book.
Your new rep: I can pressure-test the ideal-customer profile and the prep questions before meetings, so he walks in sharper. Low scope, fast, and it helps you directly.
